# SegmentedControl

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 2 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one choice out of two to five short ones, shown as a bar: a view, a mode, a range. It is a
radio group drawn as one track, so one segment is always selected. For longer choices, a
RadioGroup reads better. It is two parts: the track and its segments.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControlItem, SegmentedControlRoot } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { SegmentedControlItem, SegmentedControlRoot } from 'topclassui'

export function ViewSwitch() {
  const [view, setView] = useState('board')
  return (
    <SegmentedControlRoot value={view} onValueChange={setView} aria-label="View">
      <SegmentedControlItem value="board">Board</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="table">Table</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="calendar">Calendar</SegmentedControlItem>
    </SegmentedControlRoot>
  )
}
```

**A name and a selected segment are required.** Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and
`value` or `defaultValue`; the type refuses a track without them. Each segment is a `<button>`
with `role="radio"`, named by its own text.

**The state.** `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` are strings. Your handler runs first,
with Base UI's details, so `details.cancel()` leaves the track as it was. A server page passes
`defaultValue` alone: a handler is a function and needs a client file, as above.

**A Field's props spread onto the track** with `aria-labelledby` and a `defaultValue` beside them.

```tsx
export function ViewField(control: { id: string, name: string, required: boolean, 'aria-describedby': string, 'aria-invalid': boolean }) {
  return (
    <SegmentedControlRoot {...control} aria-labelledby={`${control.id}-label`} defaultValue="board">
      <SegmentedControlItem value="board">Board</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="table">Table</SegmentedControlItem>
    </SegmentedControlRoot>
  )
}
```

**The keyboard.** Tab enters the track on the selected segment and leaves it on the next Tab.
The arrows move to the next segment and select it, skip a disabled one, and wrap at both ends.
Under an RTL `TopClassProvider`, ArrowRight goes to the segment before. Space selects. Enter does
not, and there is no Home or End (Base UI's). Before the page hydrates the selected segment is
the one tab stop. A disabled segment is a disabled button: it leaves the tab and arrow order.

**The form.** With a `name` the form sends `name=<value>`; before the page hydrates it sends the
default. Without a `name` it is a view switch and sends nothing. **A form reset**, a reset
button or a React 19 form action that settles brings the track back to its `defaultValue` of the
latest render, on screen and in the form; a controlled track keeps its owner's value. A reset
calls no `onValueChange`. `required` never blocks a submit: a segment is always selected.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on the track: its line turns red and thickens. **`disabled`**
on the track or on a segment is the real attribute, so the form sends nothing for it.
**`readOnly`** keeps the value in the form and says so to a screen reader; it has no look of its
own.

**The look.** The selected segment is raised, with a shadow, and its text is heavier and darker;
under forced colours it takes the system highlight. The focus ring is drawn inside the focused
segment, since the track clips. Each segment is 24 px tall at least, 44 px under a finger.

**When the segments do not fit**, the track scrolls sideways inside itself and the page does
not; an arrow key brings the next segment into view. A label longer than the track ends in an
ellipsis, an element given as the label too, and text is cut at 100 characters. **`fullWidth`** fills the parent and shares it equally:
it is for a few short segments, since seven long ones on a phone are cut to nothing. In a parent
that sizes to its content (a table cell, a `w-fit` box) it is as wide as its segments.

**`icon`** on a segment is drawn before its label. It is decoration: the label names the segment.

**Where things go.** On the root, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest go to the track, the
`radiogroup`; the holder around it takes nothing. On a segment they go to its button.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Root`, `role="radiogroup"`, the arrows, Space | as they are; no `Radio.Indicator` |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names, as strings, one of the first two required; the value is held for the form reset |
| `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a segment's `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a `<span>` radio, every radio `tabindex="-1"` in the server HTML | a native `<button>`, and one tab stop in the server HTML |

### Not built

`tone` (neutral is the only one drawn), `orientation` (no vertical track), a sliding indicator,
a ring around the whole track, a toggle-group flavour that can be empty, a hover look, a
read-only look, a line around the selected segment, a skeleton (use `Skeleton`).

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  SegmentedControlRoot,
  SegmentedControlItem,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `value` on `SegmentedControlItem`. Every other prop below is optional.

### SegmentedControlRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | no | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible text names the group. |
| `aria-labelledby` | no | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the group. |
| `defaultValue` | no | `string` | - | The segment selected when the page opens, and after a form reset. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | SegmentedControlRoot: the track fills its parent and its segments share it equally. For a few short segments. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | SegmentedControlRoot: marks the choice as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the track, whose line turns to danger and thickens. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | - | The track, the element with role="radiogroup". |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | SegmentedControlRoot: the height of the track and the padding and type step of every segment; custom emits none. |
| `value` | no | `string` | - | The selected segment, held by its owner. |

### SegmentedControlItem

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | **yes** | `string` | - | The string the form receives, and what `value` and `onValueChange` of the root carry. |
| `icon` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Drawn before the label, at the size of its own. Decoration: the label names the segment. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The segment itself, which is a `<button>`. |
| `style` | no | `CSSProperties` | - |  |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
